source.title: Emergent Agentic Transformer from Chain of Hindsight Experience

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the benefit of scaling up data as motivation for combining ExoRL datasets, but does not test the language-model loss scaling laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The study reports RL benchmark returns, not held-out language-model cross-entropy, power-law fits, extrapolation of loss, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. The model-size results are qualitative ExoRL return trends in Figure 4 and are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited results from other work are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study scales offline-RL Agentic Transformer policies over four sizes (Small to XLarge) and reports environment returns. It measures no held-out pretraining loss, fits no power law, and tests no extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation or shape effect. It cites Hoffmann et al. only as motivation for pooling ExoRL datasets. The model-size return trend is a different construct (RL task return, not loss or LM downstream performance). It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude AT learns from sub-optimal trials, outperforms DT and BC, and is competitive with TD methods. They say it improves with model size and with chain-of-hindsight length, and suggest scaling model and data in future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales offline reinforcement-learning policies and measures environment returns; it does not use the original studies' language-model loss measurements or compute-allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports performance changes with model size, training and test trajectory counts, completion-token use, trajectory ordering, target return, reward-token use, and which trajectories receive loss.

fits_no_version.finding: On ExoRL Walker Stand and Cheetah Run, Agentic Transformer return rises from Small to XLarge (Figure 4). The text gives no numbers; it says AT 'improves with larger model size'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Offline-RL transformer policy return increases with model size across 2-8 layer models; no power-law form is tested.

record.code_released: The text says the code will be made publicly available; no URL is stated.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: The model-size trend is reported only in a plot with no numerical values in the text. The experiments test a small set of RL model sizes and report task returns, not language-model loss scaling laws.
record.rows_left_out: No other benchmark scores or model-variation results are included because they do not test the claim versions. Figure 1 and Table 4 report trajectory-count and configuration variations, not loss scaling, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss or power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
Sizes vary depth and width together; there is no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
Offline RL models are trained, but no power-law form is fitted to loss or return.
Returns are reported at four model sizes only in a figure, with no loss link or predictability fit. RL returns are not LM downstream tasks.
No exponents or fitting choices are compared.

record.verdict_notes: Row states of cannot_determine are appropriate, since Figure 4 values are not stated in the text. Large and XLarge share dmodel 512 and differ only in depth, so the size range is narrow (under two orders of magnitude).

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run loss fits or larger-run loss predictions are evaluated.
No fixed-compute allocation or parameter/token scaling with compute is evaluated.
The study does not compare architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Although the models are trained for reinforcement learning, the study does not test whether the same power-law form holds in that regime.

The study reports RL returns at different model sizes, but does not test downstream-task predictability from pretraining loss or establish predictable scaling of downstream performance as stated in this version.
No scaling-law exponents, fitting choices, or compute-optimal split are compared.
